item.title: Fibres All the Way Down: The Tangled Tales of Curved Spacetimes Before Einstein
item.author: hugo@example.com (Entropic Legos)
item.description:
TL;DR

While the curved spacetime of Einstein is widely known and loved, the geometrical properties of the spacetime conceived of by his predecessors is much less so. Pre-Einsteinian Spacetime, owing to the absolute nature of time, naturally endows itself with fibre bundle structure with time as the base space and Euclidean 3-space as the fibres. In this article, I attempt to give a whirlwind tour of such pre-Einsteinian conceptions in modern differential geometric parlance, going from the trivial (and “absolute”) Aristotelian bundle to the nontrivial (and “relative”) Galilean bundle, ultimately culminating in the Newton-Cartan bundle, and illustrate how this bundle gives rise to the distinctive features of Newtonian spacetime. Afterwards, I explain the geometrical differences between Newton-Cartan and Einsteinian spacetime, showing that curvature of spacetime is not something relativistic and is rather a consequence of embracing the consequences of the (weak) principle of equivalence. This isn’t a historical account of how our theories of gravity evolved - since Newton-Cartan theory actually came after GR, but an exploration of how physics might have unfolded in a universe where the language of differential geometry and fiber bundles had been spoken by Aristotle, Galileo, and Newton.

item.title: Footnotes to Veritasium - Klein-Gordon, Dirac, and More!
item.author: hugo@example.com (Entropic Legos)
item.description:
TL;DR

“God is a mathematician of a very high order and He used advanced mathematics in constructing the universe.” - Paul A.M. Dirac.

Veritasium recently released a video on the basic wave equation describing spin-1/2 fermions, AKA the Dirac equation, $$ \boxed{(i\hbar\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu - m)\Psi = 0} $$ which to me is the one of the most beautiful equations in all of physics, second only to perhaps the Einstein field equations (or perhaps Hamilton’s principle). In this post we add some technical meat that Veritasium glossed over, left unmentioned, or I thought deserves a bit more space(time), to the best of my knowledge (keeping in mind, of course, the wise words - “The equation is smarter than I am”).

item.title: The Ontological Status of Time - Preliminary Thoughts
item.author: hugo@example.com (Entropic Legos)
item.description:
TL; DR

I’m, for the time being (pun intended and very much apt), a presentist. If I find at some point that it doesn’t fit the data, I’ll drop it with no ifs and buts. I just want to see which hypothesis works better. The time hypothesis doesn’t in my opinion, as I want to make plausible in what follows. This post argues that time is not fundamental but an emergent property of change and memory. I sketch how presentism could survive relativity, reinterpret GR, and set the stage for a future quantum theory of gravity.
